ideas.title: Efficiency-ratio (Kaufman) momentum vote
ideas.mechanism: The production momentum vote is a raw 252-session price return whose magnitude is irrelevant (only its sign counts).  The Kaufman efficiency ratio ER_n = |c_t-c_{t-n}| / sum_{i=1..n}|c_{t-i+1}-c_{t-i}| is a scale-free measure of how much of the traversed path was net progress: ER near 1 in a clean trend, near 0 in chop.  Substituting it for the TSM252 vote asks the uptrend to be *efficient* rather than merely positive, which should cut the false re-entries that cost R2 its 2022-12/2023-01 whipsaw and leave the 2001/2009/2023 recoveries (all high-ER) intact.

literature.ref: Kaufman, Trading Systems and Methods (adaptive moving average efficiency ratio)
Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen, Time Series Momentum, JFE 2012 (scale-free trend strength)

ideas.title: Median-location trend vote (robust mean vs mean)
ideas.mechanism: Production's level vote is close > SMA200 -- a mean over the trailing window, which a single crash bar or a spike high biases upward for 200 sessions and which therefore holds the vote *off* too long after any single extreme print.  The median of the trailing 200 closes is the same idea with a robust location statistic; the claimed difference is fewer post-crash false negatives without any lookback change, i.e. it attacks exactly the lag the early path was invented to patch.

literature.ref: Huber, Robust Statistics (location estimators); any trend-filter survey

ideas.title: ATR/EMA channel (Keltner) vote instead of a Donchian midpoint
ideas.mechanism: DON126 asks close > the midpoint of the 126-session max/min -- a *range* channel whose width is set by the largest historical excursion, so it is insensitive to how volatile the market currently is.  A Keltner channel (EMA_n +/- k*ATR_n) scales the breakout threshold with the instrument's own current true range: in a calm market it re-enters earlier than DON126, in a wild one later, which is the opposite of the fixed-width behaviour that made R2 sit out 2009-04 and 2020-04.

literature.ref: Keltner channel / ATR (Wilder 1978); Bollinger-band breakout literature

ideas.title: Variance-ratio (Lo-MacKinlay) trend vote
ideas.mechanism: Instead of asking whether price rose, ask whether *returns are trending*: the variance ratio VR_q = Var(q-session return)/(q * Var(1-session return)) estimated on the trailing 252 sessions is > 1 exactly when multi-day returns variance-add more than linearly, i.e. when returns are positively serially dependent.  Using VR_5 > 1 (or VR_20) as the momentum vote makes the on-state conditional on the *structure* of returns rather than their level, so a positive but mean-reverting drift does not buy 2x exposure.

literature.ref: Lo & MacKinlay, Stock market prices do not follow random walks, RFS 1988
Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012 (time-series momentum)

ideas.title: Hurst-exponent regime gate on the trend vote
ideas.mechanism: The Hurst exponent estimated by rescaled range over the trailing 252 sessions is the classical persistence statistic: H > 0.5 means increments are persistent (trend friendly), H < 0.5 mean-reverting.  Gating the E2 vote (or just the early path) on H > 0.5 tests whether the strategy should be allowed to run at all in mean-reverting regimes -- the regime in which the 1935-56 and 2000-02 whipsaws live.

literature.ref: Hurst 1951; Peters, Fractal Market Analysis (R/S on equity indices)

ideas.title: Mean-reverting GARCH(1,1) volatility forecast instead of backward-looking vol20
ideas.mechanism: vol20 is the realised standard deviation of the last 20 returns: it is unbiased for the recent past and blind to the fact that volatility mean-reverts, so it under-sizes exposure exactly after a spike (when the next 20 sessions are usually calmer) and over-sizes it after a long calm stretch.  A GARCH(1,1) one-step forecast with fixed constants, sigma^2_{t+1} = omega + 0.10*r_t^2 + 0.85*sigma^2_t, omega set so the unconditional annualised volatility is 20%, is the standard term-structure-aware answer and is the only *forecast* class the record has not used (the TimesFM arm is a neural forecaster, EWMA is an exponential average with no mean reversion).

literature.ref: Bollerslev 1986 (GARCH); Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Labys 2003 (realised vol forecastability)

ideas.title: Vol-of-vol sizing (scale down when realised volatility is itself unstable)

ideas.title: ATR%-based volatility estimate (mean of true ranges, production-feasible)

ideas.title: Drawdown-depth-scaled exposure (two-sided test)
ideas.mechanism: The only state the strategy currently reacts to is vol and trend; its *own* drawdown is not a state variable.  Depth-scaled exposure multiplies the target by clip(1 - dd/D, floor, 1.0) with dd the drawdown from the 252-session high, so exposure is cut as the drawdown deepens (a risk-parity-of-losses idea), and the mirror arm *raises* it as the drawdown deepens (the recovery-value bet).  Both directions are pre-registered because dip_overlay_v1's tested trigger was a 5-day return (a fast dip), not a slow drawdown state, and the two have different trade sets.

literature.ref: Grossman & Zhou, Optimal investment strategies for controlling drawdowns, Math Finance 1993

ideas.title: Realised-skewness crash-risk scaling
ideas.mechanism: The vol target reads the second moment only.  Realised skewness of the last 252 daily returns is the third: a negative skew means the return distribution has a fat left tail, the state in which a 2x daily-reset position is most exposed to reset decay.  Arm A multiplies the target by 0.75 while the 252-session skew is below -0.5; B uses -1.0; C uses a continuous multiplier clip(1 + skew, 0.60, 1.10).  No options data is needed, unlike every tested tail measure (VIX/VXN/VIX3M).

literature.ref: Harvey & Siddique, Conditional skewness in asset pricing tests, JF 2000

ideas.title: Lag-1 return autocorrelation gate on the trend vote
ideas.mechanism: The cheapest possible serial-dependence test: rho1 = the lag-1 autocorrelation of the trailing 252 daily returns.  A trend rule should not be exposed to a 2x instrument when returns are negatively autocorrelated (a bid-ask-bounce / mean-reverting tape).  Arms: A requires rho1 > 0 for the E2 vote; B relaxes to rho1 > -0.05 (a nuisance-threshold version); C requires rho1 > 0 only for the early path.  IB04's variance ratio is the longer-horizon cousin of this; both are pre-registered so the screen can price the cheap version against the expensive one.

literature.ref: Lo & MacKinlay 1988; Campbell, Lo & MacKinlay, The Econometrics of Financial Markets, ch. 2

ideas.title: Gap-aware fill filter: do not sell into the opening gap
ideas.mechanism: Every tested fill-timing arm shifts *when* the fill happens (next close, t+2, MOC, overnight).  Untested is conditioning *whether* it happens on the fill price itself: a band-permitted downsize is skipped if the next open has already gapped more than 1% below the decision close (the sale would lock in the gap), and the ordinary rule is re-evaluated at the next close.  A/B differ in the gap threshold (1.0% / 0.5%); C applies the mirror to up-resizes (skip buying an opening gap above +1.0%). ideas.title: Tax-unit and tax-regime layer: 20/D eligibility, rate-regime switch table, income splitting
ideas.mechanism: Every arm in 80-odd studies is priced for one taxpayer under the frozen 2026 progressive tariff, and the same rule earns 11.69% after tax at $10k against 9.19% at $1M -- i.e. the *tariff*, not the rule, moves the answer by 1.5 pp.  Three things follow, none ever simulated: (a) a regime switch table that re-runs R2/A1u/H2/K under tau = 0, flat 20% and the progressive tariff on each arm's own path, which measures the rate at which K's execution layer stops paying for itself; (b) income splitting: two independent accounts of $50k (or three of $33.3k) each running K, household CAGR = the per-account CAGR, which multiplies the progressive ladder and the loss pool; (c) a routed split, where downsizes fill in whichever account's FIFO head is cheaper.  The 20/D exemption (GVK muk. 20/D, a 20-year exemption on foreign-source capital gains for individuals becoming Turkish residents from 1/1/2026) is a *precondition* answered by an adviser, not an arm: if any household member qualifies, the entire ~5 pp/yr drag moves taxpayer and the pre-tax optimum becomes the after-tax optimum.
